subject: linear-algebra
question_latex: An orthogonal projection matrix is
solution_latex: Orthogonal projections satisfy Pᵀ=P and P²=P.

subject: linear-algebra
question_latex: The determinant of a real orthogonal matrix is
solution_latex: det(QᵀQ)=det(Q)²=1.
common_mistake: Reflections have determinant −1.

subject: linear-algebra
question_latex: Which statements hold for an orthogonal projection P?
solution_latex: P and I−P project onto complementary orthogonal subspaces. P can have both 0 and 1 eigenvalues.
common_mistake: Projection rank need not equal full dimension.

subject: linear-algebra
question_latex: If P projects onto a k-dimensional subspace, trace(P) equals
solution_latex: The spectrum contains k ones and remaining zeros, so trace is k.
common_mistake: Trace equals rank for a projection.

subject: linear-algebra
question_latex: For nonzero vector a, projection onto span(a) is
solution_latex: Normalization by aᵀa makes the map idempotent and fixes a.
common_mistake: aaᵀ works only when a is unit length.

subject: linear-algebra
question_latex: Which matrix is necessarily symmetric?
solution_latex: (A+Aᵀ)ᵀ=A+Aᵀ.
common_mistake: A−Aᵀ is skew-symmetric.

subject: linear-algebra
question_latex: Enter det(Q)² for any real orthogonal square matrix Q.
solution_latex: From QᵀQ=I, determinants give det(Q)²=1.
common_mistake: The determinant itself can be −1.

subject: linear-algebra
question_latex: P is a 5×5 projection of rank 2. Enter trace(P).
solution_latex: A projection has rank-many eigenvalues 1, so trace equals rank.
common_mistake: Count both zero and one eigenvalues correctly.

subject: linear-algebra
question_latex: For P=[[1,0],[0,0]], enter the squared norm of P(3,4)ᵀ.
solution_latex: P(3,4)=(3,0), whose squared norm is 9.
common_mistake: Projection discards the orthogonal component.

subject: linear-algebra
question_latex: If Q is orthogonal and x has norm 7, enter norm(Qx).
solution_latex: Orthogonal maps preserve Euclidean norm.
common_mistake: They do not scale length by determinant.

subject: linear-algebra
question_latex: Enter rank of the 3×3 all-ones matrix.
solution_latex: Every row is the same nonzero row, so the row space is one-dimensional.
common_mistake: Nonzero entry count is unrelated to rank.

subject: linear-algebra
question_latex: P is idempotent and invertible. Enter trace(P) for a 4×4 P.
solution_latex: P²=P and invertibility imply P=I, whose trace is 4.
common_mistake: An invertible projection has no zero eigendirections.

subject: linear-algebra
question_latex: Enter the rank of diag(1,0,1,0,1).
solution_latex: There are three nonzero diagonal pivots.
common_mistake: Zeros contribute no rank.

subject: linear-algebra
question_latex: For unit a=(3/5,4/5), enter 25 times the (1,1) entry of aaᵀ.
solution_latex: The (1,1) entry is (3/5)²=9/25; scaling gives 9.
common_mistake: Outer product entries multiply coordinates.

subject: linear-algebra
question_latex: If A is 2×3 and B is 3×4, enter the number of entries in AB.
solution_latex: AB is 2×4, hence has 8 entries.
common_mistake: Inner dimensions cancel; outer dimensions remain.

subject: linear-algebra
question_latex: A 6×6 orthogonal projection has nullity 4. Enter its trace.
solution_latex: Rank-nullity gives rank 2, and projection trace equals rank.
common_mistake: Use ambient column count 6.
